rule: Eligibility: 'Severely ill or injured patients needing lifesaving, specialized care unavailable in Gaza can be medically evacuated'
note: Pathway: the Referral Committee 'decides the priority'; no priority categories or exclusion criteria stated on the page

rule: Eligibility: patients with 'serious illness, life-threatening conditions' needing continued treatment or urgent medical assistance
note: Requests from Ukraine, Moldova or EU-bordering countries are posted in the Common Emergency Communication and Information System; the note specifies no exclusion criteria

rule: Scope: specialised hospital care including emergency care and treatment for chronic diseases; 'war wounds, including civilians and soldiers'; requests for prosthetics and rehabilitation rising
note: Rare or complex diseases covered by the #ERNcare4UA initiative; trauma burns and oncology are not named as categories

rule: Hubs near airports being set up with the Commission and WHO and bordering countries; Rzeszów hub still in preparation
note: Three locations near Rzeszów (Jasionka) airport under assessment

rule: Eligibility: 'serious illnesses or life-threatening conditions that require specialised hospital services'
note: Request comes from WHO or a country in the region; participating countries then decide; no direct application to UDI; no exclusion or medical stability criteria stated

rule: Referral: foreign medical teams should 'offer to accept or refer or both accept and refer patients to other FMTs, the national health system or, if approved, other countries'
Type 2 and 3 teams must have 'a clear plan of referral to the national health system or other FMTs' when they cannot treat an emergency themselves
Transport of critically ill patients occurs 'after consultation with the host ministry of health'
'evacuation of patients to more stable parts of the country' is the only transfer option mentioned
note: The article does not discuss transfer abroad

rule: 'the most timely and cost effective response to trauma is the one mobilized by the affected country itself'
note: The part read gives no specific statement on who provides first care or when most life-saving trauma care occurs

rule: Type 1 team (outpatient initial emergency care) should arrive 'ideally within 24–48 hours'
note: Capacity at least 100 outpatients per day

rule: Type 2 team (inpatient acute and surgical care): 'it is anticipated that time to operation in the field may be several days'
note: Capacity 'at least 7 major or 15 minor operations daily'

rule: Type 3 team (complex referral surgical care, intensive care): 'unlikely to be operational in the field for at least 5–7 days'
note: At least 2 operating tables in two separate rooms

rule: 2003 WHO/PAHO guidelines call for teams to be 'fully operational within the recommended 24 hours'
note: The document says adherence has been limited

rule: Among 77 foreign field hospitals studied 'only one was operational before day three'
note: Research cited inside the WHO document; window_days_low marks day three

rule: Earthquake transfer: approximately 12,000 injured transferred to tertiary referral hospitals nationwide; the 854 assessed went to 12 referral hospitals in Tehran
note: Domestic transfer only; no statement on transfers abroad. Mortality 1.6% (n = 14); lower-extremity fractures 331 (25%); mean ISS 6.7 ±5.2; abstract also mentions 1,322 patients with injuries, relation to the 854 not clear; time after earthquake not shown in the part read

rule: Aeromedical transfer during shock stage: 'Provide that the conditions were permissive and preparation were adequate, it is safe to carry out aeromedical transportation during shock stage'
note: 4 transported in shock stage and 14 after; 1 to 6 cases per flight; 420 to 2,500 km; 1.5 to 3.5 hours; one death from multiple organ failure; timing in days after burn not reported
